items.q: What should humans learn to do instead of "doing the homework"?
items.a: People used to learn **how to do homework**; now everyone must learn to **grade the homework**. The first step in new work will be asking **ChatGPT** — the human job is **analytical verification** and **original approaches**, not repetitive execution.

items.q: What is the Stack Overflow → ChatGPT workflow?
items.a: Good engineers always **researched similar problems first**. Today that starts with ChatGPT, but you must **quickly judge whether the output is correct** — **knowledge is cheap, verification is expensive**.

items.q: What does the matchstick pyramid teach about creative thinking?
items.a: Six sticks making **four equilateral triangles** requires building in **3D** — a solution invisible on flat paper. Novel problems need **spatial/creative reframing**, not pattern-matching drills.

items.q: How does test-prep cramming kill invention?
items.a: 1980s US math competitions rewarded **unseen-problem practice**. Today's **cram industry pre-exposes every strange question**, removing surprise, killing invention, and overloading after-school hours.

items.q: What is Loh's anti-lifetime-customer-value goal for education?
items.a: Success is students who **learn to learn anything** and **stop needing classes** — *"as fast as possible, you don't need any classes from anyone ever again."* That deliberately **fails to maximize LTV**, which is the point.

items.q: Why use competition math as a thinking gym?
items.a: Algebra, geometry, combinatorics, and number theory problems are **deliberately absent from school** — chosen to practice **generating ideas**, not memorizing solutions.

items.q: How does the three-sided tutoring ecosystem work?
items.a: It unites **middle schoolers learning to think**, **brilliant high school tutors becoming polished**, and **Broadway/Hollywood-quality drama coaches** needing flexible income. Everyone must **genuinely win**, or parents reject the model.

items.q: What parent discipline governs high-school tutor tasks?
items.a: **Never ask a high schooler to do anything** unless Loh could explain to their parent why it's the **best use of their time**. Estimated US scale: **~100K HS tutors → ~1M middle schoolers** (about **1% of HS population** teaching).

items.q: How did Loh find real customer pain points?
items.a: Through **embodied discovery**: cross-country **park math talks** (50–100 attendees), overnight bus to NYC, teaching **sixth grade in disadvantaged schools**. *"You cannot create value if you don't interact with people."*

items.q: What does "everyone entrepreneur" mean in the AI Wild West?
items.a: Create value by understanding **diverse people's needs**; **intrapreneurship counts**. Growth of the live-math ecosystem was limited by **discovery speed**, not engineering — roughly **8 years to invent + 2 to scale** toward Twitch-quality streams.
